claims.claim: Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullian was a Christian writer born around 155–160 in Carthage, Roman Africa, and died after 220.
He served as a presbyter (priest) in the Carthaginian church and had a background as a Roman lawyer.
Around 211–212 AD Tertullian broke with the Catholic Church and joined the Montanist movement.
"On Fasting" (De ieiunio) was composed after his departure from the Catholic Church, probably as his third work in support of Montanism.
The treatise is addressed to the "Psychics," a term Tertullian uses for mainstream Christians who opposed the Montanist practice of additional fasts.
It was written to defend the Montanist demand for extra, more rigorous fasts against the Psychics' claim that only the biblical fast days were obligatory.
The controversy concerned whether Christians should observe only the traditional weekly and Paschal fasts or also the new, stricter fasts imposed by Montanist prophets.
The work survives in the original Latin and has been preserved in collections such as the Ante‑Nicene Fathers (volume IV) and modern translations on sites like Tertullian.org.
Scholars consider the treatise important for understanding early Christian disciplinary disputes, the Montanist movement, and Tertullian’s rhetorical method.
